James Byrd

Democratic candidate for United States Senator, Wyoming · Open seat

Retired former state legislator; previously an exploration geophysicist and IT project manager/software consultant

James W. Byrd is a former Wyoming state representative from Cheyenne who served House District 44 from 2009 to 2019 and was the Democratic nominee for Wyoming Secretary of State in 2018. He announced his U.S. Senate campaign in February 2026 for the open seat left by Sen. Cynthia Lummis, who is not running again. He won the Democratic primary on August 18, 2026, and faces Republican Harriet Hageman in the November 3 general election.

Where Byrd stands

Public lands
Opposes selling or privatizing federal public lands. Supports keeping them public under multiple-use management, with local input from ranchers, conservationists, energy workers and tribes.
Health care
Supports protecting rural hospitals and critical access designations, transparent medical pricing, caps on prescription drug costs, and making telehealth reimbursements permanent.
Energy and economy
Supports diversifying Wyoming's economy with next-generation energy such as the TerraPower Natrium nuclear project and drawing data centers to the state, while protecting traditional energy workers.
Immigration
Supports border security and enforcement along with comprehensive reform passed by Congress, including modernized visas for agricultural and seasonal labor and full funding for immigration courts to clear backlogs.
Tribal relations
Supports full, stable funding for the Indian Health Service and infrastructure investment on the Wind River Reservation, and says tribal leaders should have a seat in federal land decisions.
Senate confirmations
Says nominees should be judged on competence, integrity and respect for the law, and that qualified nominees deserve confirmation no matter which party holds the White House.
Bipartisanship
Says he will work with lawmakers of any party, citing his ten years in the minority in the Wyoming House.

Background

  • Wyoming House of Representatives, District 44 (Cheyenne), 2009–2019
  • House Minority Whip, 2013–2015; Minority Caucus Leader, 2015–2017
  • Democratic nominee for Wyoming Secretary of State, 2018 (lost)
  • Candidate for Wyoming State Senate District 8, 2020 (lost general)
  • Candidate for Wyoming House District 11, 2022 (lost primary)
  • Former exploration geophysicist for energy companies including Amoco/BP
  • Former contract computer project manager and software consultant
  • Won the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate, August 18, 2026
  • Son of Liz Byrd, the first Black woman to serve in the Wyoming Legislature
